confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion and all five PDF pages, including the references; the document has no appendix and does not state that supplementary material exists (PDF pp. 1-5).

The title and authors match the form, and the PDF identifies arXiv:2607.09018v1 [cs.HC], 10 Jul 2026; the supplied document has five pages (PDF p. 1, title, author block and arXiv stamp; complete PDF).
The paper contains one within-person experiment comparing high- and low-variance poster sets in preference and representativeness tasks; it is not a synthesis (PDF p. 2, III.B; p. 3, III.D-E).

The stimuli were manually constructed to control stylistic variance; no generative-AI assistance was assigned. The design_class other, core no, and context_class none are supported (PDF p. 2, III.B; p. 5, V, limitations).

Stimulus-set order was randomized within each task, and poster positions were randomized within the grid; task order was counterbalanced, without an explicit statement of random allocation to task-order sequences (PDF p. 3, III.D and Fig. 1 caption).

Fifty people were recruited through university mailing lists and appear in the analyzed trial totals; the same people completed both variance conditions. The per-condition counts of 50 overlap, and the study does not have fewer than 50 analyzed participants (PDF p. 3, III.C-D and Table I note; p. 5, V, limitations).

No separate participant count at randomization or participant exclusions are reported; leaving n_randomized null avoids treating the recruitment or analysis count as an explicitly reported assignment count (PDF pp. 2-3, III.B-E; p. 3, Table I note).
Each participant viewed the same 16 sets in both tasks, with eight sets per variance condition and eight posters per set; no time limit was imposed (PDF p. 3, III.D-E).

The 400 trials per variance condition in each task equal the printed 50 participants ? 8 sets per condition; the paired tests use participant-level center-selection rates, not trials as independent people (PDF p. 3, III.E and Table I note).
Preference results match the reported string and one-line finding: high variance 56% (224/400), low variance 34% (136/400), paired-samples t(49) = 3.51, p = 0.001 (PDF p. 3, Table I and IV.B).

Representativeness results match the reported string and one-line finding: high variance 66% (264/400), low variance 38% (152/400), paired-samples t(49) = 4.34, p < 0.001 (PDF p. 3, Table I; p. 4, IV.C).

Participants selected supplied designs and reported preference reasons and perceived variance; no creativity or diversity outcome was scored on participant-produced creative output. The two center-selection outcomes are correctly marked scored_on_output false and question none (PDF p. 3, III.D-E; p. 4, IV.B-C and Table II).
summary: The form accurately describes a within-person selection experiment with 50 analyzed participants and correctly reports both center-selection results. No study randomized people to generative-AI assistance or scored participant-produced creative output, so exclusion from the core dataset and context_class none are supported.
